from C code to hardware (compile/flash/execute, memory-mapped I/O, push-pull) →

slides.title: Where we are
items: Blinky runs on the on-board LED, and you can read every line that makes it blink.
Today: how that C actually reaches the hardware, a delay_ms() function that takes a time in milliseconds, and your first external circuit.
We finish by starting Lab 1 — three LEDs on a breadboard.

slides.title: AI Policy for ENGS 28
items: The course HiTA tool (in Canvas) is welcome — but work on the problem yourself first, before you ask it for help.
If you use any AI tool, disclose it in your code comments.
Test the output and make sure you understand it — you need to be able to explain every line you submit.
All comments in submitted code must be in your own words.
